title: Why AI Makes Things Up (And How to Stop It)
description: AI sometimes gives confident answers that aren't true. That's called a hallucination. Here's why it happens and three simple ways to reduce it. Follow for a new AI lesson every day. #shorts #ai #learnai #claude #aihallucination

scenes.narration: Why does AI sometimes make things up, with total confidence?
It's called a hallucination. An answer that sounds right, but isn't true.

visual.title: *Hallucination*
visual.subtitle: A confident answer that isn't actually true

scenes.narration: A language model predicts likely words. It's built to sound fluent, and it doesn't fact-check itself by default.
You can cut it down. Give it your source, let it say I don't know, and ask for quotes you can check.
For example, tell Claude: answer only from this document, and say if the answer isn't there.

visual.title: Try this prompt
items: Answer only from this document. Say if it's not there.
Got it. I'll only use the document, and I'll tell you if the answer isn't in it.

scenes.narration: And always double-check anything important, like health, money, or legal facts.
Follow for a new AI lesson every day.
